name: Input Validation Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for input validation, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for input validation, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to input validation (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. When input validation guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. When multiple input validation strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. Before starting input validation work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
5. Keep input validation changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Keep input validation outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. When input validation decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
8. Measure before optimizing any input validation bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
9. State assumptions about input validation explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated input validation concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of input validation correctness.
- Do not apply generic input validation advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new input validation abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop input validation edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about input validation over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
